# ghedata

<!-- badges: start -->

[![License: CC BY
4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-CC_BY_4.0-lightgrey.svg)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of ghedata is to share data resources that document the work of the Global Health Engineering group at ETH Zurich. The data can be used for research, teaching, and learning purposes. The data is available as an R data package, in CSV and XLSX formats.

## Installation

You can install the development version of ghedata from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("global-health-engineering/ghedata")
```

```{r}
## Run the following code in console if you don't have the packages
## install.packages(c("dplyr", "knitr", "readr", "stringr", "gt", "kableExtra"))
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(gt)
library(kableExtra)
library(ggthemes)
library(ggplot2)
```

Alternatively, you can download the individual datasets as a CSV or XLSX
file from the table below.

1.  Click Download CSV. A window opens that displays the CSV in
    your browser.
2.  Right-click anywhere inside the window and select "Save Page As...".
3.  Save the file in a folder of your choice.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

extdata_path <- "https://github.com/global-health-engineering/ghedata/raw/main/inst/extdata/"

read_csv("data-raw/dictionary.csv") |> 
  distinct(file_name) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(file_name = str_remove(file_name, ".rda")) |> 
  dplyr::rename(dataset = file_name) |> 
  mutate(
    CSV = paste0("[Download CSV](", extdata_path, dataset, ".csv)"),
    XLSX = paste0("[Download XLSX](", extdata_path, dataset, ".xlsx)")
  ) |> 
  knitr::kable()

```

## Data

The package provides access to one data resource.

```{r}
library(ghedata)
```

### people

The dataset `people` contains data about people that have worked for the group. This includes staff, as well as undergraduate student projects.

It has `r nrow(people)` observations and `r ncol(people)` variables.

```{r}
people |> 
  head(3) |> 
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::as_raw_html()
```

For an overview of the variable names, see the following table.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
readr::read_csv("data-raw/dictionary.csv") |>
  dplyr::filter(file_name == "people.rda") |>
  dplyr::select(variable_name:description) |> 
  knitr::kable() |> 
  kableExtra::kable_styling("striped") |> 
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "200px")
```

### GitHub tables

Four tables describe the work of the group on GitHub. They hold counts only and no information about who made a commit.

- `github_organisations` has `r nrow(github_organisations)` rows, one per organisation, with the number of public and private repositories.
- `github_repositories` has `r nrow(github_repositories)` rows, one per public repository.
- `github_repository_types` has `r nrow(github_repository_types)` rows with the number of repositories per organisation, visibility, type and year of creation. It counts all `r format(sum(github_repository_types$repos), big.mark = ",")` repositories, private ones and student work included, and names none.
- `github_commits` has `r nrow(github_commits)` rows, one per organisation, visibility and month, with the number of commits on the default branches. Private repositories are counted and never named.

The data was read from GitHub on `r unique(github_organisations$snapshot_date)`.

The number of repositories by type, without the `r format(sum(github_repository_types$repos[github_repository_types$repository_type == "learner repository"]), big.mark = ",")` repositories of learners in courses and workshops:

```{r github-types}
github_repository_types |>
  dplyr::filter(repository_type != "learner repository") |>
  dplyr::count(repository_type, visibility, wt = repos) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = visibility, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(total = public + private) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

`github_commit_change()` compares the commits of the last 12 complete months with the 12 months before.

```{r github-change}
github_commit_change() |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

For an overview of the variable names, see the following table.

```{r github-dictionary, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
readr::read_csv("data-raw/dictionary.csv") |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_starts(file_name, "github_")) |>
  dplyr::select(file_name:description) |>
  knitr::kable() |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling("striped") |>
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "200px")
```

## Example

```{r}
library(ghedata)

undergrad_students <- people |> 
  filter(b_m_student == "yes") |>
  filter(!is.na(thesis_title)) 
```

So far, GHE has supervised `r nrow(undergrad_students)` projects of which `r nrow(undergrad_students[undergrad_students$degree == "bsc",])` were done by BSc and `r nrow(undergrad_students[undergrad_students$degree == "msc",])` by MSc students.

```{r}
undergrad_students |> 
  count(degree, year) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n, label = n, fill = degree, color = degree)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(position=position_dodge(width=0.9), 
            vjust=-0.5,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "",
       y = "Number of students") +
  scale_fill_colorblind() +
  scale_color_colorblind() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank())
```
